overview: LiquidSense Dev's ChestStealer drains chests from a Render3DEvent that fires every frame: while a GuiChest is open and the randomized delay has passed, it shift-clicks one slot through GuiContainer.handleMouseClick, which emits C0EPacketClickWindow mode-1 packets against the chest window. Filters gate the steal: NoCompass skips while holding a compass, ChestTitle requires the container name to contain Chest, OnlyItems skips block stacks, Useful runs every stack through InventoryCleaner.isUseful, and CloseOnFull stops when the player's 36 main-inventory slots are full. The close and the silent-stealer mode are keyed off the window id reported by S30PacketWindowItems so the GUI is only released for the window the server actually opened.

sections.p: onRender3D is a render-frame handler, not a tick handler, so the steal cadence is bounded by the delay gate rather than the frame rate. nextDelay is drawn from TimeUtils.randomDelay(minDelay, maxDelay), defaults 150-200ms over a clamped 0-400ms range with cross-clamping on either value changing. In the randomized mode the module collects every stealable slot, picks one with kotlin.random.Random, and moves it, repeating in a do-while as long as the delay keeps passing, so several slots can move within one frame when the delay is at the floor. The non-random mode walks the chest rows in order and moves every slot whose gate is open. Only the chest's own rows are scanned (inventoryRows times 9), never the player's bottom slots.

noCompass returns early while the held item's unlocalized name is item.compass; chestTitle requires the lower inventory's name to contain the display name of a minecraft:chest item stack; onlyItems skips ItemBlock stacks; useful runs InventoryCleaner.isUseful(stack, -1), which classifies swords and tools against the equipped slot and rejects junk; closeOnFull reads fullInventory, true when every one of the 36 main-inventory slots is non-null. isEmpty mirrors the useful filter over the chest rows and feeds the auto-close branch. The chestTitle filter reads lowerChestInventory, which in the chest screen is the player's own inventory section titled with the fixed container.inventory string, so the contains-Chest test effectively never matches and enabling that toggle stalls the stealer entirely.

sections.h: Window id matching and silent close
sections.p: onPacket stores the window id from every S30PacketWindowItems into contentReceived. The auto-close branch only fires when screen.inventorySlots.windowId equals contentReceived and the close delay has passed, so the GUI is released only after the server refreshed the very contents the client is looking at. The silent mode (spelled slientstealer in the source) closes the GUI as soon as that match holds, which drops the chest screen before the player presses a key; because the steal gate requires a live GuiChest, clicking stops at the close. The module imports C03PacketPlayer but never references it; the only packet it actually sends is the C0E generated inside handleMouseClick.

files.label: ChestStealer.kt
files.explanation:
The whole module is two event handlers and a move helper. onRender3D performs the steal: delay gate, filter chain, slot selection, then move() which calls screen.handleMouseClick(slot, slot.slotNumber, 0, 1); that is the vanilla shift-click path and the source of every C0EPacketClickWindow the module emits. onPacket consumes S30PacketWindowItems for the window-id match that guards the close branches. The value objects cross-clamp min/max on change and redraw nextDelay so the band never inverts.

The dead C03PacketPlayer import is a telling detail: the module is pure container manipulation and never touches movement packets, so its server-side signature is a stream of window clicks, not position changes. The ChestTitle filter reading lowerChestInventory (the player inventory section) instead of the upper chest section makes that toggle effectively inert, and the silent mode is simply an early close rather than a true continue-stealing-after-close, because every handler returns when the screen is no longer a GuiChest.

files.label: InventoryCleaner.kt (useful filter)
files.explanation:
InventoryCleaner is a sibling player module whose isUseful(itemStack, slot) method ChestStealer borrows as its junk classifier. The method accepts swords and tools only when they beat the equipped item (findBetterItem against the given slot), accepts armor by type and tier, and rejects consumables and materials it considers worthless; slot -1 means the stack is not in the player's inventory, which is the case for every chest slot. The module fetches the singleton through LiquidBounce.moduleManager and calls isUseful(stack, -1) both in the steal scan and in isEmpty.

This coupling means ChestStealer's stealable set is defined by another module's value system: enabling Useful keeps the chest's garbage in place and drains only what InventoryCleaner would keep, while disabling Useful steals every non-null stack the other filters allow. The same isUseful routine drives the InventoryCleaner module's own moving, so the two modules share one classification policy.

countering.label: FastClick (window click rate)
countering.explanation:
NoCheatPlus FastClick counts inventory clicks into an ActionFrequency with five 200ms buckets against a short-term limit of 4 and a one-second window limit of 15, with lag division via TickTask. Each shift-click with an empty cursor counts 1.0; the stack-size weighting in detectTweaks1_5 only applies when the cursor already holds an item. The container-interaction path adds a violation of (155 / duration) * 100 for every click landing within 155ms of the container open time, where duration is the click timestamp minus the open timestamp.

At the stock 150-200ms delays the module lands one click per 200ms bucket (score 1-2 against the short-term limit of 4) and about 5-7 clicks per second against the window limit of 15, so the rate paths stay quiet; the first click usually lands at 150-200ms after opening, so the interact_time violation only fires when the delay draw comes up shorter than 155ms. The check turns aggressive the moment the user drops the delays: at a 50ms average the buckets carry 4-5 clicks and the window score clears 15, pushing fastClickVL toward the cancel action at vl>150 within a chest or two. The randomized mode makes things worse by concentrating pairs of clicks in single buckets, since the do-while can move several slots per frame at the delay floor.

countering.label: Open (inventory close on movement)
countering.explanation:
NCP's Open check closes the inventory when the player moves while a window is open. checkOnMove skips duplicate packets, vehicles, creative quickbar cases, merchants and vertical-velocity moves, then decides on impulse via direct WASD input where available or the movement model's hasImpulse decision; an impulse while open feeds Improbable and the caller force-closes the GUI, resetting inventoryOpenTime and containerInteractTime.

ChestStealer never touches the player's motion: the steal loop only clicks the container, so any WASD input or step while the chest is open is visible to the check, and a single impulse move aborts the drain by closing the window. The module's own filters do not guard against it, since NoCompass only reads the held item and the steal logic ignores movement state entirely. The check also resets the open-time baseline that FastClick's interact_time path compares against, so a player caught moving mid-steal loses the click-timing advantage on the next attempt.

countering.label: InventoryActions (window state mismatch)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's InventoryActions punishes ClickInventoryEvent packets when HawkPlayer.hasInventoryOpen() is zero and world interaction (InteractEntity, BlockDig, ArmSwing, InteractWorld) when it is non-zero, with a resync on every punish. Hawk tracks the window lifecycle from S2D open, C16 inventory-command and close packets, so its open state mirrors the server's window bookkeeping rather than the client's screen.

ChestStealer's silent mode is the exposure here: it calls closeScreen() as soon as the S30 window-id matches, which drops the client GUI while the server-side window is still open or just closing. Any C0E that races the close, or any click Hawk attributes to a window it already considers closed, is punished and resynced, forcing a container state refresh that interrupts the drain. The module's pure-GUI design keeps the world-interaction branch quiet, since it never swings, digs or interacts while the chest is up, but the click-after-close race is inherent to the silent close path.

countering.label: InventoryMove (rotation and state while open)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's InventoryMove check punishes rotation updates, sprinting and sneaking while an inventory window is open, excluding only teleport-accept moves, and rubberbands the player on violation. The check keys on the client's movement state as reported in the move stream, so it catches players who open a chest mid-motion or look around while the window flag is set.

ChestStealer does nothing to hide these states: it never cancels movement packets and never suppresses rotation, so a player who opens the chest while holding W or sneaking, or who turns to check surroundings mid-steal, trips the check immediately. The vanilla chest GUI normally grabs the mouse and blocks look, which is the main reason rotation-while-open is rare in legit play, but the module offers no protection for the sprint and sneak flags, which persist from the moment of opening. The randomized steal delays are irrelevant to this check, which scores movement state, not click cadence.
